newsitem.title: HONG KONG: "Boring" HK handover invitations go to world VIPs.
newsitem.headline: "Boring" HK handover invitations go to world VIPs.

text.p: It's called Asia's "party of the century", when Britain hands Hong Kong back to China, but critics say the invitations are a design turn-off.

The gilt-edged cards, at first glance almost like those for a suburban wedding, are going to world dignitaries to witness the June 30 ceremony, an historic event when a capitalist territory is freely handed to a communist power.

But the design, approved by the British and Chinese sides and featuring their national emblems, disappointed experts who called it "boring" in contrast to the gala festivities surrounding the handover of power.
"I don't think it lives up to the event," local graphic designer Karen Ma told the English-language South China Morning Post which published a picture of the downbeat card.
The invitations for the midnight ceremony are on their way to 3,600 VIPs, foreign ministers, statesmen and guests all over the world.
